### 1. What's Life Like in This Ward?
In Vadgaon Sheri - Ganesh Nagar, summer turns tin-roof homes into ovens with temperatures crossing 34°C and zero official trees to give shade. When monsoon arrives, life comes to a halt because 98% of our roads have no drains to carry rainwater away, causing immediate *pani bharaav*. On top of that, dirty water spills out into slum lanes where 8 out of 10 homes do not even have an underground sewer line.

---

### 2. Problems and What We Can Do About Them

| Problem | How Bad Is It? | Why Does This Happen Here? | What Can Be Done? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Street flooding (*pani bharaav*)** | 98.2% of our roads have no drains at all. | Rain has nowhere to go, so it fills up streets after every heavy shower. | Clean existing big *naalas* and put metal screens to stop trash from blocking water flow. |
| **Indoor heat** | Temperatures reach over 34°C, making homes unbearable. | Tin and concrete roofs soak up the sun and trap heat inside all day. | Apply white heat-reflecting paint on rooftops of 15 building clusters to keep rooms cooler. |
| **No shade on roads** | There are 0 recorded public trees and 0 parks in the ward. | Concrete roads and buildings have completely replaced open green spaces. | Put up shaded bus stops with cool drinking water and plant shade trees along a 1 km stretch. |
| **Overflowing dirty water** | 80% of slum homes lack underground sewer pipe connections. | Waste water runs into open street ditches that choke easily. | Clean the main ward drains urgently so dirty water does not mix with rainwater and back up. |
| **Wasting rainwater** | Rainwater is lost on roads while people face water shortages. | Rain simply washes away because buildings do not have storage systems. | Put rooftop rainwater collection tanks in 2 government office complexes to save clean water. |

---

### 3. How Will the Money, Workers and Time Be Used?

| Work To Be Done | How Many? | Money (Rs.) | Workers Needed | Time Needed | Who Is Responsible? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Shaded bus stops with cold drinking water taps | 12 booths | Rs. 2,160,000 | 30 person-months | 2 months | PMPML & PMC Health Department |
| White heat-reflecting paint for rooftops | 15 building clusters | Rs. 1,800,000 | 30 person-months | 1 month | PMC Building & Development Department |
| Rooftop rainwater collection tanks | 2 municipal buildings | Rs. 440,000 | 6 person-months | 2 months | PMC Water Supply Department |
| Cleaning choked *naalas* and fitting trash filters | 1 major drain section | Rs. 350,000 | 5 person-months | 1 month | PMC Drainage & Sewerage Department |
| Planting local shade trees along the roadside | 1 km stretch | Rs. 250,000 | 4 person-months | 3 months | PMC Garden Department / Tree Authority |

- **Total money being used:** Rs. 5,000,000 out of Rs. 5,000,000
- **Money left over:** Rs. 0
- **Workers needed:** 75.0 person-months
- **Everything done in:** 3 months

---

### 4. What Should the Ward Officer Do? (Step by Step)

1. **Week 1–2:** Clear out black mud and plastic trash from the main *naala* section and fit iron mesh screens so floating waste does not choke the water flow.
2. **Month 1:** Hire local painters to coat the roofs of 15 crowded building clusters with white heat-reflecting paint before peak heat hits.
3. **Month 2:** Set up the 12 shaded bus shelters with clean drinking water stations, and begin installing rooftop rainwater tanks on the 2 municipal office buildings.
4. **Month 3:** Finish planting sturdy local shade trees along the 1 km roadside stretch, install tree guards, and test all newly fitted rainwater tanks before the rains arrive.

---

### 5. How Will Residents Know Things Are Getting Better?

- ✅ After rain, streets should drain within 30-45 minutes instead of staying flooded for hours.
- ✅ Homes with white-painted roofs should feel cooler in the afternoon, making rooms livable without fans blowing hot air.
- ✅ Auto drivers, commuters, and street vendors can find cold drinking water and cool shade at 12 bus stops across the ward.
